answer: In a wildlife-data market trading grove surveys, sable sightings, and pulse readings, agents receive verification jobs in proportion to tokens bonded for 30 days, not one share per identity. Splitting a bond across a thousand accounts therefore earns no more assignments than keeping it in one. To capture a larger fraction of jobs, an attacker must acquire and immobilize proportionally more tokens, paying capital and opportunity costs for influence rather than merely inventing names.
